question: Should OpenClaw accept static `sandbox.docker.env` SecretRefs when the resolved values still become Docker environment variables visible through Docker/container metadata?
rationale: The code shape is bounded, but accepting this feature changes a credential delivery boundary on a documented Docker-visible environment surface.

options.title: Accept With Explicit Boundary
options.body: Land the linked PR only after a maintainer/security reviewer records that SecretRef-backed Docker env values are acceptable with the existing metadata-exposure warning and aligned audit/configure targets.

options.title: Require Stronger Warning First
options.body: Ask the linked PR to explicitly name SecretRef-backed Docker env exposure in docs before landing the otherwise narrow implementation.

options.title: Reject Env-Based Delivery
options.body: Pause or close the linked PR and design a non-env secret delivery mechanism if Docker metadata exposure is unacceptable for SecretRef-backed values.

recommendation.title: Accept With Explicit Boundary
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR only after a maintainer/security reviewer records that SecretRef-backed Docker env values are acceptable with the existing metadata-exposure warning and aligned audit/configure targets.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh has the strongest recent history on both explicit Docker env propagation and adjacent SecretRef runtime handling.
